thread.title: Charting a bullish September backdrop: S&P 500, Nasdaq maintain major support

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting a bullish September backdrop: S&P 500, Nasdaq maintain major support
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the major U.S. benchmarks have maintained, and rallied from, two significant support points.
Specifically, the S&P 500 has effectively nailed its breakout point (2,873) — notching a closing low within one point — while the Nasdaq Composite has maintained key trendline support, tracking slightly above the 50-day moving average.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +0.41% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, an extended retest of the breakout point (2,873) remains underway.
Delving slightly deeper, an inflection point matches the early-August peak (2,863). The S&P has thus far bottomed one point higher.
Conversely, a close atop first resistance (2,884) would strengthen the near-term backdrop.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has pulled in modestly from six-month highs.
The index is traversing a relatively tight seven-session range. Near-term support matches the range bottom (25,806) while the 26,000 mark remains an overhead sticking point.
True to recent form, the Nasdaq Composite’s near-term backdrop remains comparably weaker.
Though the index has maintained its range bottom (7,897) — closing last week (7,902) five points higher — it’s also notched three straight closes under major support (7,933).
More broadly, a headline technical test remains underway, better illustrated below.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has pulled in to trendline support from all-time highs.
The trendline is closely followed by last week’s low (7,874) and the 50-day moving average, currently 7,843. A tandem violation of these areas would raise a near-term caution flag.
Delving deeper, the former breakout point (7,806) is followed by the mid-August low (7,733). An eventual violation would mark a “lower low,” more firmly signaling an intermediate-term trend shift.
Based on today’s backdrop, the Nasdaq’s intermediate-term bias remains bullish.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is acting well technically.
The prevailing flag is a bullish continuation pattern, punctuating a shallow pullback from six-month highs.
Inflection points match the mid-August peak (25,888) and the range bottom (25,806), areas better illustrated on the hourly chart.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has pulled in to the breakout point (2,873) and survived the initial retest.
Also recall that last week’s low (2,864) matched a floor at the early-August peak (2,863).
The bigger picture As detailed above, the bigger-picture backdrop has thus far weathered two headline technical tests.
To start, the Nasdaq Composite has maintained a five-month uptrend, rising modestly from support this week.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has initially maintained the breakout point (2,873), rising from last week’s close one point under support.
The quality of both rally attempts, still underway, will likely add color.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF IWM, +0.25% has also maintained major support.
The specific area matches the breakout point (170.20) and the small-cap benchmark has registered three straight closes fractionally higher.
Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P MidCap 400 remains comparably stronger than the Russell 2000.
Tactically, the breakout point (366.70) is closely followed by the 50-day moving average (365.25) and the slightly deeper trendline. The MDY’s intermediate-term bias remains bullish barring a violation.
Against this backdrop, the Russell 3000 Index is also acting well technically. This a comprehensive benchmark, encompassing about 98% of U.S. market capitalization. (Or about 98% of U.S. stock market value.)
Put differently, the Russell 3000 reduces the disproportionate influence of mega-caps, including for instance Apple, Amazon and Alphabet.
Notably, the Russell 3000’s August breakout registered as powerful, encompassing three consecutive closes atop the 20-day Bollinger bands, also known as volatility bands.
As always, consecutive closes atop the bands are statistically unusual — as recently detailed — and distinctly bullish for the longer-term . See the July rally atop the bands, and subsequent follow-through higher.
Still, the index was near-term extended at the August peak, and a healthy consolidation phase is currently underway.
Perhaps more usefully, the Russell 3000’s backdrop contradicts a recently popular bear-case argument that the prevailing rally is precariously narrow. (Recall that the S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF’s backdrop, detailed last week, also signals that the prevailing rally is broadly-enough based.)
Returning to the S&P 500, the index has initially maintained its first notable support.
To reiterate, last week’s low (2,864) closely matched the early-August peak (2,863). Separately, the S&P’s closing low (2,872) has thus far registered one point under the breakout point (2,873).
As always, technical price action within an uptrend is constructive.
Delving deeper, inflection points match the July peak (2,848) and the ascending 50-day moving average, currently 2,834. The S&P 500’s intermediate-term technical bias remains bullish barring a violation.
See also: Charting a bull-trend pullback, S&P 500 digests rally atop 20-day volatility bands.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Profiled last week, Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN, +1.29% has pulled in from a headline milestone.
Recall that the shares briefly tagged the $1 trillion value mark last week — on an intraday basis — defined by a share price of 2,050.27.
Amazon topped last week at 2,050.50 — just 23 cents higher — and has since pulled in from record territory.
Tactically, Amazon’s first notable floor matches the breakout point (1,921), detailed previously. Tuesday’s early session low (1,917.00) has closely matched the breakout point, as well as trendline support, and has initially drawn buyers.
A deeper floor matches the July peak (1,880) and Amazon’s intermediate-term bias remain bullish barring a violation.
Moving to U.S. sectors, the iShares Transportation Average ETF IYT, +0.00% has taken flight.
As illustrated, the group has staged a bull-flag breakout, reaching all-time highs amid a volume spike.
More broadly, the upturn punctuates a multi-month continuation pattern — illustrated on the three-year chart — opening the path to potentially material follow-through. An intermediate-term target projects to the 216 area.
As an economically-sensitive sector, the group’s persistent strength supports the bull case.
Synopsis, Inc. SNPS, -0.06% is a large-cap developer of electronic design automation (EDA) software products used to test integrated circuits.
Late last month, the shares knifed to record territory, rising amid a volume spike after the company’s third-quarter results.
The ensuing pullback has been comparably flat, positioning the shares to build on the August spike. Tactically, a near-term floor closely matches the September closing low (100.70) and a sustained posture higher supports a bullish bias.
Cognex Corp. CGNX, -0.13% is a large-cap developer of machine vision products.
The shares initially spiked six weeks ago, gapping higher after the company’s second-quarter results.
More immediately, the shares have closed fractionally atop the 200-day moving average, currently 53.70, for the first time since March. The upturn marks a five-month high, laying the groundwork for potentially more decisive follow-through.
Medtronic plc MDT, -0.04% is a well positioned large-cap medical device manufacturer.
As illustrated, the shares have recently gapped to record territory, rising after the company’s strong quarterly results.
More broadly, the shares are well positioned on the three-year chart, rising from a multi-year base. Tactically, a near-term floor matches the September low (95.10) and is followed by the firmer breakout point, an area roughly matching trendline support. (See the 90 area on the three-year chart.)
Public since October 2017, CarGurus, Inc. CARG, +3.58% is a well positioned large-cap name.
Technically, the shares have recently gapped to record territory, punctuating a steep August break atop the March peak.
The subsequent pullback has been comparably flat, placing the shares at an attractive entry near gap support and 12.9% under the August peak. Consider that the September low has registered just six cents above the top of the gap (46.55).
